chunks: Ali, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'The Tasbeeh (glorification) is half the scale, and 'Al-hamdu lillah' (praise be to Allah) fills the scale, and 'Allahu Akbar' (Allah is the Greatest) fills what is between the sky and the earth.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Amir al-Mu'minin (Commander of the Faithful, referring to Imam Ali)
key_terms.الْمِيزَانِ: The Scale (of deeds on Judgment Day)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual weight of Tasbeeh, Tahmeed, and Takbeer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi highlights the metaphysical weight of the triad of dhikr, where 'Subhanallah' (Glory to God) serves as the foundational half of the moral scale, 'Al-hamdu lillah' (Praise to God) completes it, and 'Allahu Akbar' (God is Greatest) transcends earthly limits to fill the cosmos. In Shia scholarship, this is often interpreted not merely as quantitative merit but as a qualitative transformation of the soul, aligning the believer’s consciousness with divine attributes of transcendence, gratitude, and supremacy. The narration underscores the practical importance of these specific phrases in daily devotional practice as a means of balancing one's spiritual ledger.
